description: IBCS horizontal pin chart (EX 1.1 card 8, UN 4.1): relative variance ΔPY% / ΔPL% per period as thin pins with square heads (AC solid, FC hatched), colour = impact (good / bad / neutral), variance axis in the reference scenario's notation, N/A where the relative variance cannot be interpreted.

fields.Period: text, category label; sort the visual by period ascending
fields.AC: measure, actual; BLANK where there is no actual
fields.PL: measure, plan/budget (refScenario 'PL'); any other code works the same way, e.g. BU: bind it under that name and set refScenario = 'BU' (plan notation: two-line axis)
fields.Polarity: optional measure 1 / -1 / 0; else the polarity knob
fields.BU: measure, budget (refScenario 'BU'); plan notation like PL
fields.YMin: optional measure (fraction, ≤ 0), same on every row: lowest Δ% the axis must show; wins over yMin
fields.YMax: optional measure (fraction, ≥ 0): highest Δ% the axis must show; wins over yMax
fields.PxPerUnit: optional measure, same value on every row: px per percentage point of this chart's pin scale (sized to its plot: 0.9 × plot height ÷ clipped range, or the value shared with charts read together); wins over pxPerUnit
fields.ClipPct: optional measure (fraction > 0), same on every row: |Δ%| beyond which a pin is an outlier; wins over clipPct

ibcs.notes: ΔX% = (AC-REF)/REF with the SIGNED reference (never ABS). N/A when REF is blank or 0, or when REF < 0 and naOnNegativeRef is true (IBCS UN 4.1 p.54). If you pass a precomputed ΔPY% measure instead, keep the same rule in DAX. Same % scale on the page: the same pxPerUnit (px per percentage point) on every pin chart and each visual's height sized to its own Δ% range (usermeta.ibcs.layout), not the same yMin/yMax on visuals of one height. Rows with a blank Period are dropped (a constant measure such as a scale field would otherwise add a blank category). Rounded-zero rule: a variance that rounds to 0 at `decimals` is labelled 0 without sign and gets no impact colour. Outliers (UN 5.3, CH 4.4): set clipPct (fraction, e.g. 0.5 = 50%) or bind ClipPct for business-irrelevant relative outliers: the pin is cut at that value, has no head, keeps its full label, and a small triangle beyond the label points in the growth direction. Only for relative variances; never cut absolute columns or bars (CH 2.1). Outlier pins (OURS): a pin whose |Δ%| exceeds pinOutlierFactor (3) × the next-largest |Δ%| of the tier, or the ±clip (default ±100 %), whichever is smaller, is an outlier: the tier is scaled from the other pins and the outlier is clipped at that limit with the outlier triangle and its full label. Reason: one immaterial reference (AC 0 against a budget that rounds to 0 gives −100 %) would otherwise set the scale and flatten every other pin. Differing % scales are marked (OURS, UN 5.2 / CH 4.3): this chart's pin scale is sized to its own tier, so when it differs from the page's other pin tiers set pinScaleBand (-1 = auto round value 1/2/5 × 10^n % at 25–60 % of the tier; or the same fraction in charts read together): a band at the left edge of the plot from the axis with its value label, the tier name moves to the other side of the axis; scale_layout.py sets -1 whenever the page's pin scales differ, and the page footnote says the % tiers are on different scales.

layout.rule: container height = fixedPx + (hi − lo) × pxPerUnit + padHigh + padLow; measured with Vega-Lite 6.4.3 at ibcsFontSize 12 ; with an outlier (clipPct) add ibcsFontSize + ibcsPinHeadMax + 6 px to padHigh and padLow (the triangle beyond the label); the pin tier has its own % scale: scale_layout.py sets pxPerUnit (px per percentage point) to 0.9 × pinTierPx ÷ the pin range (member pinTierPx = this chart's plot height, default 48), shared only with charts aligned through alignTiers

previewVariants.note: pinScaleBand -1: a scaling marker at the left edge for a % scale that differs from the page's other pin tiers.

pinOutlierFactor 3 (default): Apr has AC 0.0 against a budget of 0.04 (rounds to 0.0), so ΔBU% = −100 %; it is more than 3 × the next-largest |Δ%|, so it is clipped at that limit with the outlier triangle and its full label, and the other pins (about ±2 %) keep their length.

params.name: refScenario
params.description: reference scenario: 'PY' or a plan code such as 'PL' or 'BU' (any code except PY gets the two-line plan axis); the field of that name must be bound

params.name: decimals
params.description: decimals for the relative-variance labels (the token format with this precision); default 1, the same in Power BI and web apps (number.format.relativeVariance1)

params.name: polarity
params.description: used when the Polarity field is absent: 1, -1 or 0. Overridden per row by a Polarity field.

params.name: periodType
params.description: year | quarter | month | week | day: category width per period type (UN 3.3)

params.name: stepScale
params.description: screen scaling of the token category step; keep it identical on every page

params.name: yMin
params.description: lowest relative variance the scale must show, as a fraction (-0.3 = -30%); 0 = from the data

params.name: yMax
params.description: highest relative variance as a fraction (0.3 = +30%); 0 = from the data. A shared DOMAIN: same yMin/yMax gives the same % scale only on pin charts of the same height. To share one pin scale with charts read together use pxPerUnit instead

params.name: pxPerUnit
params.description: px per percentage point (1% = 0.01) on the value axis; 0 = off. When set, the domain is the plot height ÷ pxPerUnit, anchored at the lowest pin (plus label room), so every pin chart of the page shows the same px per % point. Size the container to the data (usermeta.ibcs.layout, scripts/scale_layout.py of the ibcs-power-bi skill). If the container is too small, the data wins and the px per point shrinks: nothing is cut

params.name: showCategoryLabels
params.description: false hides the category labels, e.g. for a tier stacked directly above another visual that already shows them

params.name: clipPct
params.description: relative outlier clip (UN 5.3, CH 4.4) as a fraction; default 1 = ±100 % (ours, the same rule in Power BI and web apps): pins beyond it are cut at the clip point, have no head, end in a triangle in the growth direction at the clip point and keep their full label; 0 = off (field ClipPct wins)

params.name: pinOutlierFactor
params.description: outlier rule for pins (OURS): a pin beyond pinOutlierFactor × the next-largest |Δ%| of the tier is clipped there (outlier triangle, full label) and does not set the tier's scale; the ±clip still applies when it is smaller. 0 = off (only the ±clip)

params.name: pinScaleBand
params.description: scaling marker of the pin tier (UN 5.2, CH 4.3; OURS rule): required when this chart's % scale differs from the page's other pin tiers (each pin tier is sized to its own tier; only charts read together, the months and their Total, share one). -1 = auto: a round value 1/2/5 × 10^n % that is 25–60 % of the plot height; a fraction (0.1 = 10 %) = that value, the same in charts read together; 0 = off. A band at the tier's start in the scale-band colours with its value label; scripts/scale_layout.py sets -1 when the page's pin scales differ; the page footnote says the % tiers are on different scales

params.name: naOnNegativeRef
params.description: show N/A when the reference is negative

params.name: ibcsLabelPad
params.description: label room beyond the longest pin, as a share of it (pxPerUnit = 0)

params.name: ibcsLabelPx
params.description: label room in px beyond a pin head, both directions (pxPerUnit > 0 only; else ibcsLabelPad)

params.name: bw
params.description: column width: 2/3 of the category, capped at the token step so every chart of this period type has the same width

params.name: stemPx
params.description: pin stem: token ratio × column width, clamped in px (geometry.pin.stemPx)

params.name: headPx
params.description: pin head edge: the token minimum (geometry.pin.headPx.min, 6 px), small against the stem so the stem length carries the value

layer.description: selection (cross-filtering): assisting-area band behind every mark of the selected category; no mark is dimmed (a dimmed AC reads like PY)
AC -> FC separator: a short tick on the category axis between the last AC and the first FC period (the same as the web components), never a line through the tiers, so no label crosses it
variance axis: PY = solid light thick line
variance axis: PL/BU = two thin parallel lines

pin body: thin, impact colour, in front of the axis; geometry follows the arithmetic sign; an outlier is cut at the clip value (UN 5.3); a non-zero pin is at least head + 2 px long (the head never covers the stem); a Δ% that rounds to zero keeps its head on the axis as a baseline marker
white ground under hatched FC heads
pin head: square in the minuend's scenario notation (AC solid dark, FC hatched)
labels outside the head, in the direction of the change; N/A on the axis
outlier marker (UN 5.3, CH 4.4): headless pin cut at the clip value, a triangle at the clip point pointing in the growth direction, impact colour; the label keeps the full value beyond it

scaling marker (UN 5.2, CH 4.3; OURS): with pinScaleBand, a narrow light band at the left edge of the plot from the axis to a round % value, so a % scale that differs from the page's other pin tiers is visible
scaling marker line at the round value
scaling marker label: the round value beyond the band end, secondary text colour at label size
tier label (ΔPY% / ΔPL%) left of the axis; below the axis when the scaling marker grows upwards from it
